## What this module is, and what it is not

A whole-buffer LZ4 codec with a streaming adapter over `std.Io`. The block API decodes into a caller's slice whose length is the output
budget (`LZ4_decompress_safe`'s contract) and compresses with a single-probe hash-table greedy
matcher at LZ4's default level, with LZ4's acceleration knob, or (`hc_level` 3..12) with the HC matcher; either may take a dictionary. The frame API reads everything an
`.lz4` file may hold — LZ4 frames with every combination of the descriptor flags and block sizes,
skippable frames, legacy frames, concatenated in any order — into a fresh allocation (`decompress`) or a
caller's buffer whose length caps the output (`decompressInto`), and writes one LZ4 frame with the
options liblz4's `LZ4F_preferences_t` offers (the compression level is `acceleration` for the fast matcher, `hc_level` for HC).

**HC levels.** `CompressOptions.hc_level` / `EncodeOptions.hc_level` 3..12 select a hash-chain matcher: levels 3..9 with lazy matching (a longer match one or two bytes on replaces the one found; the skipped bytes become literals), `2^(level+1)` chain links per probe; levels 10..12 with an optimal parser (liblz4's `LZ4HC_compress_optimal` idea): a dynamic programme over the next 2048 positions prices every way to reach each one (a literal from the previous position, or a match of any length from an earlier one) in the bytes the format spends (token, two offset bytes, literals, the length bytes past 15) and commits the cheapest path; offsets all cost two bytes, so one longest match per position stands for every shorter length at it; a match of 64 / 128 / 4096 bytes (liblz4's target lengths) is taken without weighing it; 96, 512 and 16384 chain links per position (liblz4's own counts; this chain search gets less out of each link than liblz4's finder, so levels 10 and 11 come out larger than `lz4 -10` / `-11` while level 12 reaches its size; measured on a 400 KB text sample by `tools/dict_oracle.py`: our block 55214 / 49399 / 49073 bytes against `lz4 -10/-11/-12` frames of 51449 / 49156 / 49033, that is 7.3 % over at level 10, 0.5 % over at 11 and 0.1 % over at 12, while 3..9 are within a few percent of `lz4 -3..-9`; at level 10 our block is larger than our level 9 on this sample). 0..2 are the fast matcher, above 12 is 12. The tables (about 192 KiB, and about 100 KiB more of parse state at levels 10..12) live on the stack for `compressBlock` / `compressInto` and in an allocation for the `gpa` forms. The output is the ordinary block format: every decoder reads it.

**Dictionaries.** `compressBlockDict` / `decompressBlockDict` take the bytes before the block (the last 64 KiB - 1 count, as in liblz4's `LZ4_loadDict`; the encoder seeds its table with every third byte of it as liblz4 does, the HC matcher inserts all of it); `compressDict` / `decompressDict` do the same for frames: the header carries an optional 4-byte Dictionary ID, linked blocks use the dictionary as the history of the first block of each frame, independent blocks each start from it (liblz4's `LZ4F_compressBegin_usingDict` semantics, `lz4 -D`). The id is written, never compared: knowing which dictionary a frame needs is the caller's job, as in liblz4. They allocate scratch (dictionary tail plus the block or input) and `decompressInto` takes no dictionary. Checked in both directions against python-lz4 `dict=` and `lz4 -D` (`tools/dict_oracle.py`).

**Streaming.** `Compressor` is a `std.Io.Writer` (`init(gpa, out, options)`, `finish`) that writes one frame block by block, its `writer.buffer` being the block: memory is the history window plus one block of input and one compressed block, linked blocks slide the window, HC rebuilds its chain table per block from the history. `flush` on the writer emits a short block. `Decompressor` is a `std.Io.Reader` (`init(gpa, input, buffer, options)`) over concatenated LZ4 frames and skippable frames: one compressed block, one decoded block and the history window; a malformed stream is `error.ReadFailed` with `err` holding the `DecodeError`; `max_output`, `verify_checksums` and `dictionary` as in the one-shot decoder. Legacy frames are not read by the streaming decoder (`BadMagic`; the one-shot decoder reads them).

**Not here (expected by some, deliberately absent):** writing legacy
frames, the `lz4` command-line program.

## Wire format / algorithm

- **Block** (lz4_Block_format.md): sequences of `token` (high nibble literal length, low nibble
  match length − 4; 15 = more length bytes follow, each added, until one is not 255), literals,
  a little-endian 16-bit offset (1..65535) and the match length extension. The last sequence holds
  literals only and the block ends right after them (rule 1). Matches may overlap their own output
  (offset < length repeats a pattern).
- **Frame** (lz4_Frame_format.md): magic `0x184D2204`; FLG (version `01`, block independence,
  block checksum, content size, content checksum, reserved bit, dictionary id), BD (block maximum
  size id 4..7 = 64 KiB, 256 KiB, 1 MiB, 4 MiB; other bits reserved), optional 8-byte content size
  and 4-byte dictionary id, header checksum `(xxh32(descriptor, 0) >> 8) & 0xFF`; blocks as a 32-bit
  size word (high bit = stored uncompressed), data, optional xxh32 of the stored bytes; the end mark
  `0x00000000`; an optional xxh32 of the content.
- **Skippable frame:** magic `0x184D2A50..5F`, 32-bit length, payload — skipped.
- **Legacy frame** (`lz4 -l`): magic `0x184C2102`, then 32-bit compressed sizes and independent
  blocks of at most 8 MiB each, until the input ends or a word over `LZ4_COMPRESSBOUND(8 MiB)`
  takes the place of a size (every frame magic number is; that word is read again as the next
  frame's magic, or as trailing data — the lz4 CLI's "maybe new stream?").
- **Compressor:** 4-byte sequences hashed (`v * 2654435761`, the top bits) into a 16 KiB table: a
  single block shorter than 65547 bytes (liblz4's `LZ4_64Klimit`) keeps 8192 u16 positions (13 bits,
  liblz4's `byU16` table), anything else (a frame, a larger block) 4096 u32 positions; on a miss
  the step grows by one every 64 misses (× acceleration), LZ4's skip; a hit is extended backwards
  over pending literals and forwards eight bytes at a time; after a match the position two bytes
  before its end is entered. The last match starts at least 12 bytes before the block's end and the
  last 5 bytes are literals (rules 2 and 3), so liblz4 accepts every block. In a linked frame the
  hash table carries over and matches reach up to 64 KiB into the previous blocks. In an
  independent frame every block starts without history, as liblz4's (`LZ4F_compressBlock` →
  `LZ4_compress_fast_extState_fastReset`, which clears its table or moves its base 64 KiB on): the
  table is not cleared, but an entry from an earlier block is below the block's start and refused
  on its probe exactly as an empty slot is, so the output is the same as with a cleared table. A block that
  does not shrink is stored (as liblz4 does).

## Behaviour choices (owner rule: like the reference or the majority; the spec's mandate first)

| Question | Choice | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Offset 0 | `error.BadOffset` | Format: "0 is an invalid offset value … denotes an invalid (corrupted) block". liblz4 1.10.0 instead zero-fills the match and accepts (measured); the spec's mandate wins. |
| End-of-block rules 2 and 3 (last 5 bytes literals, last match ≥ 12 bytes before the end) | Not enforced by the decoder; always obeyed by the encoder | Format: "a conformant decoder is allowed to reject the block". liblz4's safe loop enforces them relative to its output capacity, its fast loop does not in the same way, so its verdict is not a clean rule; lz4_flex does not enforce them. `tools/interop.zig` shows every block liblz4 refuses and we accept breaks one of them. |
| Rule 1 (block ends after a literal-only sequence), empty block | Enforced: `error.Truncated` / `error.CorruptBlock` | Format; liblz4 refuses both (measured: `LZ4_decompress_safe("", …)` = −1). |
| Match-length nibble of the last token | Ignored | Format (no match follows); liblz4 the same, except at output capacity 0 where it accepts only the byte `0x00`. |
| Concatenated frames | Read all (`multi_frame = true`) | lz4 CLI and lz4_flex read them. `multi_frame = false` reads the first frame only and makes anything after it `error.TrailingData` (Arrow IPC's "exactly one frame"); python-lz4 reads the first and ignores the rest, which is `multi_frame = false` with `ignore_trailing_garbage = true`. |
| Junk after the last frame | `error.TrailingData` (`ignore_trailing_garbage` to accept) | lz4 CLI exits with an error (output written); python-lz4 ignores it. |
| A word over `LZ4_COMPRESSBOUND(8 MiB)` after a legacy frame's blocks | Ends the legacy frame; read again as a magic number, so junk there is `error.TrailingData` (ignored with `ignore_trailing_garbage`) | lz4 CLI 1.10.0 `LZ4IO_decodeLegacyStream`: "Cannot read next block : maybe new stream ?", then `selectDecoder`'s "Stream followed by undecodable data". |
| Empty input | Empty output | lz4 CLI (exit 0) and lz4_flex; python-lz4 raises. |
| Skippable frames | Skipped, anywhere | lz4 CLI, liblz4 frame API. |
| Legacy frames | Read, in any order with other frames | lz4 CLI reads them (and, measured, fails on a legacy frame *after* an LZ4 frame — an artefact of its decoder, not followed); liblz4's frame API, python-lz4 and lz4_flex do not read them. |
| Dictionary id in the header | Read and ignored; `decompressDict` applies the caller's dictionary to every frame whatever the id | liblz4 (measured: decodes such a frame; `LZ4F_decompress_usingDict` does not compare ids); lz4_flex refuses it. |
| Content size field 0 | "Unknown", not checked | liblz4 (measured). |
| Content size mismatch, stored or decoded block over the block maximum, reserved bits, version ≠ 01, block size id < 4, header checksum | Errors | liblz4 (measured, each), lz4_flex (size, block maximum). |
| Block and content checksums | Verified (`verify_checksums = false` skips) | liblz4, the CLI (`--no-crc` skips), lz4_flex. |
| Encoder defaults | 64 KiB, linked blocks, no checksums, no content size | liblz4's zeroed `LZ4F_preferences_t` (python-lz4: the same plus content size; the CLI: 4 MiB independent blocks with a content checksum). |

## Constant-time contract

None claimed: the data is public. There is no secret in this module.

## Limits and refusals

- `decompressBlock`: output at most `dst.len` (`error.OutputTooSmall`); no history.
- Frame block maximum: from BD (64 KiB … 4 MiB); a stored block, a compressed block's size word or
  its decoded size over it is `error.BlockTooLarge`. Legacy blocks: at most 8 MiB decoded
  (`error.BlockTooLarge`) and `LZ4_COMPRESSBOUND(8 MiB)` stored (a larger word ends the frame).
- Match lengths are summed with an overflow check from their 4-byte minimum on, so a long run
  of 255 bytes in a raw block cannot wrap the length on a 32-bit target.
- `DecodeOptions.max_output`: default 256 MiB (`default_max_output`), `null` = unbounded; one byte
  more is `error.OutputTooLarge`; a header whose content size exceeds what is left of the cap is
  refused before its blocks are read (pinned by `test "frame: the output cap"`).
- Allocation: a compressed block reserves `min(block maximum, 255 × stored size, cap left)` (no
  block decodes to more than 255 bytes per stored byte); nothing is sized from a declared length.
- Compressor input: at most `0x7E000000` bytes per block (`max_block_input`, liblz4's
  `LZ4_MAX_INPUT_SIZE`) and `2^32 − 1` per frame (`error.InputTooLarge`); `acceleration` is clamped
  to 1..65537 as in liblz4.
- Bounds: `compressBlockBound(n) = n + n/255 + 16` (liblz4's macro); `compressBound(n, opts)` = the
  header, `n`, 4 bytes per block (+4 with block checksums), the end mark (+4 with a content
  checksum).

## Speed

Bench: `tools/bench.zig` (`zig build bench-lz4`), `compressBlock` / `decompressBlock` over 64 KiB independent blocks of three
8 MiB payloads against `lz4 -b1 -B65536` (liblz4 from the distro). The figures are the card's `Performance` line
(ratio = our time / liblz4's, ours padded against the Intel JCC erratum with `-Djcc-safe`, as the card's convention asks for
ratios near 1.0; the distro `lz4` cannot be padded). Unpadded, the decoder's loop is sensitive to where its branches fall
against 32-byte boundaries and the same code can be well behind (B6).

The techniques, each kept with an instruction-count A/B and a bench run (liblz4's `lz4.c` read as the design reference for
the techniques, no code copied; see NOTICE):

- **Decoder fast loop with a hand-back.** While more than 16 input bytes and 64 output bytes are
  left, a sequence is copied in whole chunks: 16 literal bytes at once, a match at offset ≥ 16 in
  16-byte chunks, a shorter offset as a 16-byte pattern (lanes `i % offset`) stored every
  `offset · ⌊16 / offset⌋` bytes. Any sequence it cannot take within its margins — a length that
  runs off the input, an offset outside the window, a long literal or match too near an end — goes
  back to its token, and the exact tail loop decides the rest of the block. The fast loop so has no
  error path and no call; every verdict is the tail loop's (pinned by a test that cuts a block at
  every byte and its output at every size near the end, against the byte-at-a-time model).
  liblz4 jumps into its safe loop mid-sequence; the rewind is the same idea without `goto`.
- **Long matches out of line.** The rest of a match over 32 bytes is copied by a separate function;
  inlined, its unrolled loop took the registers of the short-match path, which then spilled.
- **liblz4's `byU16` table for a small block** (`compress` under 65547 bytes): twice the entries in
  the same 16 KiB. The parse is liblz4's, which also makes our blocks faster to decode.
- **Encoder output without per-byte checks.** A sequence is written unchecked when the room left
  holds its worst case (lengths bounded by `n >> 7`) plus 16 bytes, and through the checked writer
  otherwise (liblz4 drops its checks altogether when the output holds `LZ4_COMPRESSBOUND`).
  Literals go in 8- and 16-byte chunks instead of `memcpy`; the 8-byte chunk's overshoot is always
  overwritten by the offset and the block's last sequence, so nothing past the output changes
  (pinned by a test at every capacity around the compressed size).
- **The next probe's hash read before the current probe is judged** (liblz4's `forwardH`), and the
  backward extension out of line: inlined, LLVM stepped a dozen values derived from `ip` with its
  loop.

## Verification

`scripts/modtest lz4` runs the unit tests and the fuzz harnesses' fixed seeds; `zig build interop-lz4` (needs the `lz4` CLI
and python3 with python-lz4, `tools/README.md`) and `zig build bench-lz4` are the live comparisons. Test classes (`src/`):
- **Blocks** (`block.zig`): hand-built sequences, malformed blocks as typed errors, history-prefix reach and the fast loop's
  offset check, encoder capacity (same bytes or `NoSpaceLeft`, nothing written past the output), the u16 table up to
  liblz4's 64 KiB limit, `compressBlockBound` against liblz4's macro, round trips over shapes and accelerations, the
  end-of-block rules the encoder always obeys, the 13-byte minimum and the window edge, acceleration trading size for speed.
- **Frames** (`frame_test.zig`): stored and compressed blocks, header refusals, content-size agreement, block-size limits
  per block maximum, block and content checksums, xxHash32 against the values the CLI writes, linked and independent blocks
  (a match never reaches into the previous frame; every independent block decodes alone), malformed compressed blocks,
  truncation anywhere, concatenation / skippable frames / trailing data, legacy frames (including a block at exactly
  `LZ4_COMPRESSBOUND(8 MiB)`), the output cap (exactly one block maximum, a declared size over what is left), content
  checksums of concatenated frames, `decompressInto`, encoder options and header bits, stored incompressible blocks.
- **Goldens** (`golden_test.zig`): the CLI's frames replayed against the recorded inputs, and every damaged byte of a
  checksummed frame caught.
- **Fuzz** (`fuzz_test.zig`): three harnesses run by testkit's deterministic driver, `LZ4_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]`
  (names `lz4-decode`, `lz4-block`, `lz4-roundtrip`): the frame decoder never panics, leaks or hangs and its verdict and
  bytes (`decompress` and `decompressInto`) equal an independent frame model's; the block decoder agrees with the
  byte-at-a-time block model; encode then decode is the identity. A fixed set of 3000 seeds runs in every test run and
  its reach is checked; a separate test cuts blocks at every byte and every output capacity near the end against the model.
- **Live interop and goldens' producers** (`tools/`): see Anchoring. The block model and the frame model are the
  re-derived anchor.
- **Mutation:** schemata over `src/block.zig` and `src/frame.zig`, one mutant per guard and class (drop, flip, off by one,
  the other arm, skip an assignment, error remap), over the decoder fast loop, `wildMatch`, `copyLong` and the encoder's
  sequence writer, search loop and back-extension too. The surviving equivalents are cost-only or ratio-only (the fast
  loop only changes speed; the encoder's parse is free within the format) or unobservable (an input over 2 GiB).
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module mutation run and the delta runs after it.

## What is deliberately not done

- **Byte parity with liblz4's compressor** — not claimed: the format leaves the matcher free. A single block under 65547 bytes uses liblz4's hash, table layout, skip and
  search order, and the bench payloads compress to the same sizes as `lz4 -1` (text and runs equal,
  noisy text 2 bytes longer of 4.6 MB); the last probes before a block's end follow a different
  rule (ours probes every position up to `end − 12`, liblz4 stops when the next one would pass
  `end − 11`), so the bytes are not pinned against liblz4 and no test claims they are equal.
- **Enforcing end-of-block rules 2 and 3 in the decoder** — not now (see Behaviour choices); a
  strict mode could be added if a consumer needs to refuse what liblz4 refuses.
- **Writing legacy frames** — never: `lz4 -l` exists for old Linux kernels' boot images; reading
  them is enough.

## Backlog / deferred

- *BOUNCED (quiet-host):* **B6** Speed, what is left (not attempted in wave 14: a perf claim needs interleaved ReleaseFast A/B runs
  with a spread below the effect, and the benchmark queue was shared with other agents' jobs, so a spread
  that small could not be had): (a) the decoder's loop is a JCC-erratum layout lottery on
  Skylake-family hosts (well behind liblz4 unpadded across builds of nearly the same code, level with it
  padded; the card's Performance line has the figures); crc32c fixed the same thing with its hot loop as one aligned inline-asm block, which
  for a decoder with a dozen bound checks per sequence is a larger and riskier change. (b) Frames
  and blocks of 65547 bytes and more keep the 4-byte hash into 4096 u32 positions; liblz4's
  `byU32` path hashes 5 bytes on 64-bit targets (`LZ4_hash5`), which changes frame output and was
  not measured. (c) No corpus beyond the three generated payloads (no Silesia-like files).

## Open

- Big-endian and 32-bit targets are not run; `meta.targets` is `linux64`.
